questions.question: Explain the difference between a need and a want, giving two examples of each.

points.text: A need is essential for survival (food, water, shelter, clothing). A want is desirable but not essential (mobile phone, holiday, branded clothing). Needs are limited; wants are unlimited - this creates the basic economic problem of scarcity.

questions.question: Describe the four factors of production and explain how they work together in a business.

points.text: Land = natural resources (oil, farmland, water). Labour = human effort (workers' skills and time). Capital = man-made resources used in production (machinery, tools, factories). Enterprise = the entrepreneur who organises the other factors and takes risks. questions.question: An entrepreneur is considering leaving a secure job to start a business. Discuss the risks and rewards of this decision.

points.text: Risks: loss of regular income, personal savings invested, stress of uncertainty, possible business failure (20% of new businesses fail in first year). Rewards: potential for higher income, independence and flexibility, personal satisfaction, building an asset, creating jobs. A balanced answer weighs both and concludes with a justified view.
